subject: business-studies
title: Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet
welcome_lead: Read the two core financial statements like a CFO.
meta_desc: A-Level Finance: income statement (P&L) and statement of financial position.
final_note: Profit measures performance over a period; the balance sheet shows position on a date.

concepts.def: Income from sales over a period.
Resources the business owns or controls.
Owner's claim on the business: assets minus liabilities.

walkthroughs.body_html: The P&L runs from revenue down to net profit: deduct cost of sales for gross profit, deduct operating expenses for operating profit, deduct interest and tax for net profit.
The balance sheet on a single date lists non-current and current assets, current and non-current liabilities, and equity. By definition assets equal liabilities plus equity.
Firms can manipulate the balance sheet at year-end - paying suppliers early, delaying invoices - to flatter ratios. Analysts use multi-year trends to detect window dressing.

options: Revenue minus cost of sales
Gross profit minus operating expenses
Revenue minus tax
Net profit plus interest

options: Income statement
Cash flow forecast
Balance sheet

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
